summary: Purpose: repair toolchain orchestration without automatic Knowledge-authority publication; W0/TWR-W0: typed source selection (consumer, policy, module, resource-set, authority, path/module IDs), independently verifiable projected read set and selection identity, fail closed on omission/ambiguity/authority drift; W1/TWR-W1: adapter owns deterministic chunking, pagination, offsets, bounded retries, continuation binding to selection and source identity; W2/TWR-W2: adapter proves byte/line/hash coverage, rejects gaps, conflicting overlaps, byte changes, and model promotion of incomplete reads; W3/TWR-W3: independent execution, publication, and semantic-review gates, allowing verified degraded successor for unchanged semantics while blocking invalid LKG, selection/authority drift, missing sources, integrity failure; no automatic Bootstrap or Knowledge publication; W4/TWR-W4: validator/coordinator owns immutable receipts in versioned generations, binding candidate, contract, registry, authority envelope, Skill-input receipt, Knowledge freeze, validator identity; current typed pointer advances only after validation, replay reuses or byte-identically succeeds, invalid generations cannot become current; W5/TWR-W5: attempts under .skill-input-work/<plan-id>/<attempt-id>, lifecycle states, leases/heartbeats, retention protections; dry-run candidates, apply requires explicit maintainer approval and emits non-authorizing cleanup receipt with candidates/protected objects/reasons/bytes/predecessor commit; W6/TWR-W6: non-authorizing end-to-end test covers selection through retention, resolves one current pointer, rejects invalid advancement; ownership: VDD draft/plan-ready, Maintainer implementation authorization, Quick Dev implementation-complete, Acceptance acceptance-passed; no new lifecycle authority.
